series: BASH REDIRECTION: THE FIELD MANUAL — PART 2

slides.page_title: The Whole Manual on One Page (cont.)

items: `<<EOF` expands the body, `<<'EOF'` keeps it literal.
`<<-EOF` strips leading tabs; `<<< "str"` is the one-liner.
`<(cmd)` is a filename you read from.
`>(cmd)` is a filename you write into — neither seeks.
Stages stream concurrently with buffer backpressure.
SIGPIPE ends the producer once the consumer quits.
Status is the last stage unless `set -o pipefail`.

lines: # and remember: `| head` will now trip it

caption.text: Part 2 of BASH REDIRECTION: THE FIELD MANUAL. `2>&1 > file` and `> file 2>&1` look like the same command typed in a different mood — one files both streams, the other leaves stderr on your terminal. This 10-page field manual walks the fd table from `dup2` up through heredocs, process substitution and `pipefail`, so you can read any redirection left to right and know exactly where every byte goes. Save it for the next time a cron job swears it succeeded.
